findings.evidence: deltaSequence uses only Polynomial.Sequence, multichoose, composition and coefficient mapping; its degree proof uses the Baker degree theorem and no interpolation declarations.
findings.fix: Move and export the scaled delta sequence in Baker/Delta.lean with an application formula; relocate its leading-coefficient result at line 154 alongside it.
findings.issue: The private deltaSequence packages a reusable polynomial sequence independently of Waldschmidt interpolation, preventing consumers from using its basis and degree API.

findings.evidence: Repository-wide rg finds only eval_waldschmidtDelta_mem_range_intCast; its proof at lines 132–133 manually rewrites waldschmidtDelta_def, map_prod, eval_polynomial_aeval and eval_X.
findings.fix: Add a @[simp] evaluation formula expressing the value as the product of the mapped binomial-polynomial values at q * x i, and use it in the integrality proof.
findings.issue: The evaluation API proves integrality but provides no formula computing eval x (waldschmidtDelta q τ), forcing consumers to expand its defining polynomial representation.

summary: The delta-polynomial interface hides reusable sequence infrastructure and lacks a characteristic evaluation lemma.
